notes: The pipeline's drafting brain, wired at last - and deliberately narrow. Until now every outreach email was the same deterministic template you edited by hand, which is why it read like a bulk mailer. Switch the drafting mode to 'model brain' and each draft costs exactly one model call: the model writes the message itself, reacting to what that person actually wrote, while the product appends the opt-out line, the signature and the postal address - so compliance is the product's job, not something a model can forget. The person's text is treated as untrusted data, the call carries no tools, and the recipient is never chosen by the model, so an injected instruction can at worst change text you read before sending. The hard rules reject rather than repair: an address that is not the recipient's, executable markup, an empty or over-long body - all fall back to the template with the reason recorded on the draft. A model error is a soft fallback too, and it never retries, because a retry is another bill. The cost has its own cap, separate from the send cap, because a model call costs money even when the draft is never sent; today's drafts and their tokens are metered, and an incomplete provider usage reads '?' rather than a made-up number. Off by default, and with no model configured nothing is built and no call can happen. No new credential, no new outbound path - it uses the model endpoint you already have.
